cases.description: The published unit registry passes structural and semantic validation.
Unit IDs are unique within a registry snapshot.
Physical conversion multipliers are strictly positive.
Affine conversion definitions are restricted to temperature.
Every derived physical unit names an existing base unit.
Physical conversion definitions cannot form a cycle.
A physical dimension has exactly one registry base unit.
Case-insensitive alias sets cannot contain equivalent forms.
An active unit cannot redirect to a replacement.
A deprecated unit names an existing active replacement.
Every active unit provides at least one parser alias.
Registry label and alias languages use well-formed BCP 47 tags.
Every physical unit definition cites a standards or official-guidance source.
A unit has at most one alias set for a language and case-sensitivity policy.
US customary measures, sums, alternatives, notes, and references are valid.
Australian cup and tablespoon identities remain regional.
Metric ranges, approximation, and opaque quantities are valid.
Independent sections, package size, alternatives, and extensions remain valid.
Independent pastry, filling, finish, and assembly structures remain valid.
Cross-component assembly and a counted spice with a physical length remain lossless.
Opaque measures, packet sizes, and multi-stage bowl assembly remain valid.
A vessel-dependent quantity remains explicitly unresolved.
Mass-based hydration, package size, fermentation, and ingredient reuse remain valid.
An ambiguous Canadian cup remains opaque while known metric amounts remain structured.
Per-item mass, staged oven settings, an internal target, and exact, ranged, and approximate timing assertions remain distinct.
A ranged half-power microwave interval carries its source rating while the following standing time remains unannotated.
An Arabic recipe with Latin unit abbreviations names its English translation by recipe ID.
An English translation names its Arabic original and differs from it in steps, IDs, and notes.
The stable temperature-purpose vocabulary and a labeled unusual purpose are valid in one ordered step.
Ordered temperature ranges survive without becoming scalable recipe amounts.
A negative freezer setpoint remains a canonical signed temperature.
Non-English Unicode recipe content and localized sections remain lossless.
Ingredient temperature, approximate yield, cooking range, and opaque lower-bounded chilling time remain distinct.
Two steps preserve distinct authored uses of one divided ingredient.
An ingredient without an amount or unit is valid.
Ordered authored equipment names may carry ordinary quantities and notes without IDs or step references.
Equipment order, authored names, quantity forms, notes, and scoped extensions survive a read and write cycle.
Every equipment entry preserves a nonempty authored name.
A temperature describes a condition rather than an equipment quantity.
Ordered name-only, person, organization, and labeled other author credits are valid without inferred identity.
Ordered recipe images, a primary selection, and a shared recipe/step image resolve through explicit asset references.
A step ingredient use may carry an authored quantity or only a reference.
An alternative option may preserve a non-recursive sum of simple quantities.
Container count and per-container physical size remain distinct.
A registered grandfathered BCP 47 language tag is accepted.
Every difficult ingredient line satisfies its expected and prohibited inferences.
Exact, affine, approximate, ranged, incompatible, nonphysical, and unknown-unit conversions match the registry.
Every resolution vector reaches its specified identity, unresolved outcome, or reported conflict from the decisions it supplies.
Unknown extensions and their opaque JSON payloads survive at their original object scopes.
Author order, omitted and explicit kinds, labels, URLs, and scoped extensions survive independently from source provenance.
Source identity, application-scoped identifier, attribution, and supplementary retrieval time survive a round trip.
A retrieval timestamp records an event but does not identify a source.
An unscoped source-system identifier does not identify a portable source.
A source-system identifier names its application or format namespace.
Temperature-purpose order, known kinds, labels, absent purpose, and scoped extensions survive a read and write cycle.
Opaque temperature wording and its optional purpose survive a read and write cycle without numeric inference.
Recipe image order, a non-first primary image, shared step imagery, asset roles, and scoped extensions survive a round trip.
Omitted approximate and explicit false are semantically equivalent for amounts and normalized durations.
Ingredient-use order, optional quantities, quantity forms, and scoped extensions survive a read and write cycle.
Authored recipe variants survive a read and write cycle with their order, titles, and text, including an untitled variant and one that refers to another variant in prose.
A variant in a document declaring a newer format version preserves an unknown future standard member and a well-formed scoped extension, without admitting the recipe members forbidden by section 6.7.
Variants do not nest or compose.
A variant preserves authored content and is not shorthand for an embedded recipe.

Authored ingredient optionality survives a read and write cycle, is scoped to the ingredient occurrence rather than the ingredient identity, and is kept distinct from unquantified, serving-purpose, and preference ingredients.
Ingredient optionality is a boolean assertion, not free text.
Authored step titles survive independently from section titles and authoritative instruction text.
A step title labels but does not replace authoritative instruction text.
Simple and sum alternative options preserve their order and shallow structure through a round trip.
Distinct authored classifications and date- or timestamp-precision source chronology are valid.
Classification order and publication chronology precision survive a read and write cycle.
An authored classification array does not repeat one exact label.
Publication chronology uses an RFC 3339 full date or date-time rather than localized prose.
A date-shaped publication value must also be a real calendar date.
The unreleased string author form is replaced by one canonical object representation.
Every author object has a credited name.
Author kinds use the intentionally small standardized vocabulary.
An authored kind label refines only the other author kind.
An author URL is absolute rather than relative to an importing location.
An alternative option cannot itself be another alternative.
A sum inside an alternative still accepts only simple terms.
An extension name carries two reversed-domain labels and one or more local labels, at any depth within the length limits, including in the reserved x-sref.spec namespace.
An extension name without a collision-resistant reverse-domain namespace is invalid.
Two labels name a domain and nothing within it, so the name identifies no particular extension.
Every label begins and ends with a letter or digit, so an empty label is invalid however many labels surround it.
An extension resembling a required core member does not satisfy that requirement.
A recipe without the required format version is invalid.
A decimal string cannot be used as a normalized rational.
A newer compatible recipe with unknown standard members and a future registry ID remains readable and preserves opaque data at every scope.
A newer compatible recipe version with the current registry preserves unknown standard members at the document, section, ingredient, and step scopes.
The current recipe version with a newer compatible registry preserves unknown unit IDs in simple, range, sum, alternative, yield, package-size, and temperature positions.
A recipe from another format compatibility line is rejected explicitly.
A recipe naming a registry from another compatibility line is rejected explicitly.
A normalized fraction must be reduced.
A range minimum cannot exceed its maximum.
Ingredient IDs must be unique across every ingredient section.
Every step ingredient reference must resolve in the recipe.
Every step ingredient use identifies the ingredient it describes.
A step cannot contain multiple uses of the same ingredient.
A temperature unit cannot describe how much of an ingredient a step uses.
Every standard unit ID must exist in the selected registry.
A reader rejects an object that repeats a member name.
A reader rejects nonfinite numeric tokens even inside an extension.
Recipe language and source locale values use well-formed BCP 47 tags.
Step IDs are unique across all instruction sections.
Ingredient section IDs are unique within a recipe.
Instruction section IDs are unique within a recipe.
A whole number is serialized as an integer rather than with denominator one.
Normalized rational components fit in the unsigned 64-bit interoperability bound.
Human-readable text excludes prohibited C0 control characters.
The primary image resolves to an asset with an image media type.
Every recipe-level image reference resolves to an asset in the same recipe.
A recipe-level image reference cannot resolve to a non-image asset.
Recipe-level image references are unique while retaining authored order.
Asset IDs are unique within a recipe.
Asset paths are unique within a recipe.
Asset paths cannot contain empty, current-directory, or parent-directory segments.
The primary image is selected from the recipe-level image references.
Asset roles cannot duplicate the explicit primary-image relationship.
Asset roles cannot duplicate explicit step-image relationships.
Ingredient and step temperature fields use registered temperature units.
One temperature assertion cannot be both numeric and opaque.
A signed temperature rational cannot use negative zero.
A temperature unit appears only in a dedicated temperature field.
A temperature unit cannot describe the size of an item or package.
A temperature unit cannot describe recipe yield.
A structured temperature purpose always names its standardized kind.
An unusual purpose uses labeled other rather than extending the stable kind vocabulary.
The other temperature-purpose kind carries source terminology in a label.
A package size is expressed in a physical unit.
Extracted, inferred, and unresolved normalization retains source text.
Inferred and unresolved normalization explains the remaining uncertainty.
A complete declared asset with digit-leading portable IDs and matching digest and size is valid.
A declared asset missing from the archive is invalid.
A regular archive file absent from the manifest is invalid.
Asset bytes must match the declared SHA-256 digest even when size is unchanged.
Asset bytes must match the declared size.
Recipe bytes must match the manifest digest and size.
Recipe and manifest asset declarations must agree exactly.
Manifest asset IDs and paths are each unique.
A package manifest cannot repeat its version member.
A package manifest cannot repeat an integrity-bearing recipe digest member.
A package manifest contains exactly one complete JSON value.
Archive entries cannot escape the package root with parent segments.
Archive entry names use forward slashes only.
Archive entry names are relative to the package root.
Archive entry names cannot use a platform drive-letter prefix.
Archive entry names cannot contain control characters.
Archive entry names cannot contain empty path segments.
A package cannot repeat an archive entry name.
A package cannot contain symbolic links or other non-regular members.
A package contains exactly one root manifest.json.
A package contains exactly one root recipe.json.
The required recipe entry contains valid UTF-8 JSON.
A package reader enforces a finite compression-ratio limit before extraction.
Malformed archive bytes are rejected without extraction.
Exact, approximate, ranged, and opaque duration expressions coexist with canonical timing identities, shared references, and independent summaries.
Rated output, selected watts, explicit percentages, opaque levels, and nonheating intervals remain distinct.
One opaque authored schedule and its ordered power/time choices, restrictions, source wording, and unknown scoped data survive a round trip.
Selected watts, percentage, and opaque wording are exclusive representations of one power setting.
An explicit operating percentage is greater than zero and at most 100.
An authored alternative schedule retains its complete opaque duration rather than becoming a range.
A choice schedule does not also claim one shared power condition.
Power/time choices have distinct source conditions.
A translation names its original by title, a later translation by bundle-local recipe ID, and an alternate by URL.
Relationship order, relations, languages, titles, recipe IDs, URLs, and a scoped extension survive a round trip.
A relationship identifies its counterpart by title, recipe ID, or URL.
A relationship is original, translation, or alternate.
A counterpart's language is a well-formed BCP 47 tag.
A recipe declares at most one original.
A recipe that declares translations states its own language.
A relationship does not name the recipe's own ID as its counterpart.
A timing classified as other requires authored presentation text.
A newer compatible release cannot add a timing kind outside the compatibility line's frozen closed set.
Every canonical timing assertion has recipe-local identity.
A timing assertion without a duration expression says nothing and is invalid.
One duration expression cannot be both normalized and opaque.
Authored timing attention is active, passive, or unstated.
A step refers to one timing assertion at most once.
A recipe timing summary uses a duration expression rather than a scalar duration string.
Timing assertion identities are unique within a recipe clock.
Timing order, duration expressions, labels, step references, attention semantics, source text, and scoped extensions survive a read and write cycle.
A step cannot refer to a timing assertion the recipe does not contain.
A step image reference resolves to an image asset in the same recipe.
A step image reference cannot resolve to a non-image asset.
Step image references are unique while retaining authored order.
An ordered bundle with a digit-leading member ID whose members are each complete, independently valid packages.
A bundle manifest cannot repeat its format member.
A bundle manifest cannot repeat an identity-bearing member ID at any nesting depth.
A bundle manifest contains exactly one complete JSON value.
A declared member the archive does not carry.
A package below recipes/ that the manifest does not declare.
A root file other than the manifest.
A member of the declared size whose bytes were altered.
A member longer than the manifest declares.
Two independently valid packages with the same recipe-local ID and distinct bundle member IDs.
A bundle recipe entry without its required bundle-local member identity.
One bundle-local member ID declared twice.
A member named by application convention rather than by its recipe ID.
A verified member carrying a different recipe than the manifest claims.
A member whose digest verifies and whose package is incomplete.
A bundle declaring no recipes.
A generation timestamp is prohibited because it introduces container variation unrelated to recipe content.
A bundle with members and no manifest.
A member path that escapes the archive root.
A file with the bundle suffix that is not an archive.
A package for a recipe with no assets, whose manifest still declares an empty `assets` array.
`assets` is required even when the recipe declares none.
A manifest states the package version it was written to.
The package version is a constant, not a range.
The recipe entry names `recipe.json` and nothing else.
The recipe entry declares `application/json` and nothing else.
The manifest's member set is closed, so a writer cannot add one to it.
`format` is a constant, so another value is another format.
A bundle manifest says what it is before anything reads it.
The bundle manifest version is a constant, and a later one is not this one.
The bundle manifest's member set is closed.
A package's recipe names a unit absent from the registry it declares, which a reader refuses to load and a writer refuses to produce.
A bundle member's recipe names a unit absent from the registry it declares, which makes the member an invalid package and a reader refuses the bundle.

A bundle writer refuses to produce a member whose recipe names a unit absent from the registry it declares. This fixture is byte-equivalent to the reader case but separately indexed so each processor boundary has its own requirement ID.
A package carrying text, SVG and binary assets, so an asset a reader cannot treat as text survives the round trip.
A package whose recipe carries extension members, which a writer must return unchanged without understanding them.
A package whose recipe declares a newer format version and carries unknown standard members at several depths, all of which must survive the container.
A package whose recipe declares a newer unit registry and uses unknown registry IDs across the quantity shapes, which must be preserved rather than resolved.
A bundle of three members - one with assets, one minimal, one carrying extensions - so member order is more than a swap and mixed members share one bundle.
Two members declare each other as language alternates by recipe ID; each remains a complete package on its own.
A rendition with a different step structure from its counterpart names it by recipe ID.
A document declaring 0.1.0 carries an unprefixed root member 0.1.0 does not define, which a reader refuses and a writer refuses to produce.
The same rule inside an ingredient, so the vocabulary is scoped by version at every object depth rather than only at the root.
The same rule inside a step.
A newer unit registry does not widen the recipe member vocabulary: the registry and recipe compatibility lines are independent.
The converse: a newer recipe version does not admit an unknown registry ID, which stays an unknown unit.
Recipe minimum: ingredients-only.
Recipe minimum: instructions-only.
Recipe minimum: neither-collection.
Recipe minimum: empty-ingredient-collection.
Recipe minimum: empty-instruction-collection.
Recipe minimum: null-ingredient-collection.
Recipe minimum: null-instruction-collection.
A package preserves a recipe with one authored collection.
A package preserves a recipe with one authored collection.
A bundle preserves ingredients-only and instructions-only recipes.
Complete shallow branches preserve identity, different quantities, scoped notes and optionality, authored relationships, and step uses.
Choice relationships, branch IDs and extensions remain scoped during round trips.
A choice requires at least two branches.
A choice branch cannot be another choice.
Quantities belong to complete branches, never the choice.
Authored relationships do not define Boolean logic.
A choice declares its authored relationship.
Every complete branch has an authored name.
Choice and branch IDs share the ingredient namespace.
Whole-choice references cannot assign an ambiguous amount.
A complete authored-choice example.
Four independently authored yields, one approximate, one ranged, and one opaque, need not convert into one another.
Per-serving, per-100 g, whole-recipe, and unspecified nutrition statements keep authored zero, approximation, ranges, opaque values, and a unitless value.
Separate dietary claims and allergen declarations keep presence, precaution, absence, conditions, and a variant scope.
Ingredients name the recipes that make them by title and URL, by bundle-local recipe ID, and by title alone; each stays unresolved without error.
One asset carries creator, credit, rights, license, and source URL; one carries only a credit that names no creator; one carries no provenance, so its license is unknown.
Yield order and apparently equivalent yields, nutrition bases, authored zeros, opaque values, unitless values, and scoped extensions survive a round trip.
Claim order, conditions, variant scope, and asset provenance survive a round trip.
SREF 0.4 records yields as an array; a singular yield member is not defined.
A yields array is nonempty.
Energy uses kcal or kJ.
A nutrient other than energy uses a mass unit.
A quantity basis states its quantity.
An unspecified basis carries no quantity.
An opaque nutrient value carries no amount or unit.
A nutrient of other carries a label.
A basis kind is recipe, serving, quantity, or unspecified.
A nutrition statement lists at least one nutrient.
A statement lists a nutrient and label once.
A temperature unit cannot describe a nutrition basis.
A dietary claim states suitable or unsuitable.
A diet outside the normalized subjects stays in the claim text.
A bare allergen name is not a declaration; presence is required.
Presence is contains, may_contain, or free_from.
An allergen declaration names its substance.
A claim scoped to a variant names an existing variant ID.
Variant IDs are unique.
A recipe dependency identifies the other recipe by title, recipe ID, or URL.
A recipe dependency does not name the recipe's own ID.
An asset license has a name, a URL, or both.
An asset source URL is absolute.
